narrative: Native and near-native French speakers are required to consult with the Undergraduate Advisor before enrolling for the first time in any French course in order to verify placement.

MAJOR REGULATIONS
PREREQUISITES Check the General Catalog for the prerequisites to all listed courses.
P/NP GRADING OPTION Not allowed for major courses (prep or UD major), including courses applied to the major from other departments.
SUBSTITUTIONS In the major requirements permissible only by petition to the department chair and dean.
G.P.A REQUIREMENTS At least 2.0 overall UC average in all upper-division major courses and all courses (Prep and UD) for the major.
DOUBLE MAJORS With the approval of each department chairperson, up to a total of 8 units may be applied simultaneously to both UD majors.

groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Courses not in French Department

nodes.title: Paris and Rome in the Nineteenth Century
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Courses not in French Department
nodes.prereq_text: Not open to freshmen.
nodes.description: Comparative history of how two great cities were transformed from pre-modern to modern; focus on architecture and design as well as politics, economics, and culture; emergence of new ideas about the very concept of "the city."

nodes.title: Architecture, Planning, and Culture in Eighteenth-Century Paris
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Courses not in French Department
nodes.prereq_text: Not open to freshmen.
nodes.description: Paris (and Versailles) from the Sun King to the Revolution, rococo, neoclassicism, origins of urbanism; extensive use of primary texts in translation to study architectural debates in the press and their connection to contemporary political battles.

nodes.title: Elementary French
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower Division French Requirement
nodes.description: Introductory course for students with no prior exposure to French. Grammar, vocabulary, speaking, reading, and writing taught entirely in French through interactive presentations and activities. Exposure to French and Francophone culture is a hallmark of the program. Four days a week.

nodes.title: Elementary French
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower Division French Requirement
nodes.prereq_text: French 1.
nodes.description: A continuation of French 1. Targets students' developing knowledge of the fundamentals of French language, focusing on speaking, reading, and writing abilities through a focus on French and Francophone culture. Meets four days a week; in French.

nodes.title: Elementary French
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower Division French Requirement
nodes.prereq_text: French 2.
nodes.description: A continuation of French 2. By course end, students are exposed to the fundamentals of French and have acquired a solid working vocabulary. Writing and speaking encouraged through class discussion and web-based and creative projects. Four days a week; in French.

nodes.title: Intermediate French
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower Division French Requirement
nodes.description: First in the three-quarter intermediate French series. Builds on foundation established in first-year and includes thorough review of French grammar. Speaking and writing skills developed through exposure to French and Francophone culture, literature, and film. Four days a week; in French.

nodes.title: Intermediate French
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower Division French Requirement
nodes.prereq_text: French 4.
nodes.description: A continuation of French 4. Discussion encouraged through oral reports on such topics as Impressionist art and French film. Readings include poetry, plays, and short stories. Web-based activities add to the interest of the course. Four days a week; in French.

nodes.title: Intermediate French
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower Division French Requirement
nodes.prereq_text: French 5.
nodes.description: Continuation of French 5. Students complete their grammar review. Continued emphasis on speaking and writing through an examination of contemporary French culture, with exposure to some of the important trends in French intellectual history, notably Existentialism. Four days a week; in French.

nodes.title: Intermediate French for Global Studies and Political Science
groups: PREPARATION FOR THE MAJOR: Lower Division French Requirement
nodes.prereq_text: French 5 or equivalent.
nodes.description: Students complete review of French grammar. Continued emphasis on speaking, reading, and writing through study of French and Francophone history, politics, language policy, and culture within a global and larger European context. Four days a week; in French.

nodes.title: Foundations of French and Francophone Culture
nodes.description: An introductory, interdisciplinary approach to the literary and cultural history of France and Francophone world from the Middle Ages and the Renaissance. Readings of poetry, drama, and fiction. Focus on advanced discussion and writing in French.

nodes.title: Foundations of French and Francophone Culture
nodes.description: An introductory, interdisciplinary approach to the literary and cultural history of France and Francophone world from the seventeenth century and the Enlightenment. Readings of poetry, drama, and fiction. Focus on advanced discussion and writing in French.

nodes.title: Foundations of French and Francophone Culture
nodes.description: An introductory, interdisciplinary approach to the literary and cultural history of France and the Francophone world from the nineteenth to the twenty-first century. Readings of poetry, drama, and fiction. Focus on advanced discussion and writing in French.

nodes.title: Critical Writing in French
nodes.prereq_text: French 6, 6GS, or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: This advanced composition course focuses on enhancing students’ analytical skills through an examination of French argumentative modes and critical reading of texts (literature, journalistic essays, political and philosophical works). The goal for students is to develop a clear, persuasive argument on specific works and major issues both orally and in writing. Course includes a comprehensive analysis of complex grammatical structures and the enhancement of French vocabulary for a range of communicative contexts.

nodes.title: Writing the Self
nodes.prereq_text: French 6, 6GS, or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: Readings in twentieth-century autobiography serving as models for creative writing. Coursework involves analysis of literary works and a long-term ‘autobiographical project’ that may be factual or fictionalized. Course includes a practice of complex grammatical structures and the enhancement of French vocabulary.

nodes.title: Advanced French Grammar
nodes.prereq_text: French 6, 6GS, or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: Course is designed to provide a thorough review of the rules of French grammar and to situate the discussions within linguistic and cultural contexts, covering topics such as semantics, syntax, and inclusive writing. Explores linguistic features and political contexts of domestic and global varieties of the language. Additional foci include continued vocabulary enrichment, increased syntactic accuracy, and composition skills in French.

nodes.title: Business Communication and Cultural Affairs
nodes.prereq_text: French 6, 6GS, or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: Study of specific vocabulary, formulae, and writing strategies useful for individual career objectives in the business world. Students will acquire a foundation in contemporary business and professional French, developed through the analysis and application of business concepts and the composition of analytic essays and business documents.

nodes.title: Finance and Marketing in French
nodes.prereq_text: French 6, 6GS, or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: Students study essential aspects of the conduct of business in France, as well as specific features of the French language, both spoken and written, commonly encountered in business practice. Prepares students to take the (optional) competency exam for the Diplôme de français professionnel B2, which is offered annually by the Chambre de Commerce et d'Industrie de Paris (CCIP). The continuation of Business French 1, but not limited to students who have taken that course.

nodes.title: Conversational French
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: FR 6 or equivalent
nodes.description: Concurrently offered with French 116A, this two-unit version offers ongoing opportunities to speak French. Students prepare the oral and written work (interviews, readings/videos, short quizzes, assiduous class participation), but are dispensed from such major assignments as the extensive oral presentation.

nodes.title: Rhetoric of Social Change
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: French 100.
nodes.description: From a transhistorical perspective (medieval to modern times), the study and analysis of French and Francophone authors who sought to change the world through their writings (political, legal, journalistic, literary, educational, etc.). In French.

nodes.title: Greatest French Speeches
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: One course from French 104A-B-C-E-F, or French 6 with an A grade or above.
nodes.description: Rhetorical analysis of the history, theory, and practice of public speaking in France through texts and videos of great speeches that shaped French and Francophone culture (and beyond). Students also practice delivering their own speeches. In French.

nodes.title: Intensive French Conversation
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: Fr 6, French 6GS, or equivalent.
nodes.description: Concurrently offered with French 106, this four-unit version includes such assignments as oral interviews, readings/videos, short quizzes, and assiduous class participation; in addition to which, each participant leads the discussion in an extensive presentation on a subject of their choice.

nodes.title: Public Speaking in French
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: One course from French 104A-B-C-E-F or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: Participants develop multiple opportunities to practice eloquent oral communication in the French language (e.g. for the classroom, sociopolitical advocacy, the workplace). Extensive work in rhetorical analysis provides the basis for their own enhanced professional fluency and development. In French.

nodes.title: French and Francophone Poetry
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.description: Study of poetic materials and technique. Analysis of the masterpieces of French poetry, including the French Renaissance with the cole de Lyon and the Pliade; Romanticism; Symbolist, Cubists, and Surrealist aesthetics. Content will vary from quarter to quarter. In French.

nodes.title: French and Francophone Theater
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.description: Study of the French theater from the seventeenth century to the present, with plays by Molire, Beaumarchais, Hugo, Musset, Ionesco, Beckett, and other playwrights. In French.

nodes.title: French and Francophone Prose Fiction
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: 1 course from French 101A-B-C, or equivalent, (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: Introduction to the techniques of literary analysis for prose fiction. Study of the novel as a cultural form staging the major transformations in French-speaking literature and culture in the broad context of European and World history. In French.

nodes.title: Literary Translation: Theory and Practice
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: 1 course from French 104A-B-C-E-F, or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: Exploration of the various theories of translation. Offers a practical component where students work on a specific translation project. Examination of literary, philosophical, linguistic and theoretical texts by Jakobson, Benjamin, Steiner, Derrida and others.

nodes.title: The French Enlightenment
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: 1 course from French 101A-B-C, or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: A reading of basic Enlightenment texts, stressing the fundamental works of Rousseau, Voltaire, Diderot, Laclos, and other major figures of the century. Lectures and reading in French.

nodes.title: Reading Paris (1830-1890)
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: 1 course from French 101A-B-C, or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: This course explores the literary and artistic representations of Paris and its Haussmannization. In works by Balzac, Baudelaire, Zola, Manet and the Impressionists, we explore the painting of modern life, Paris as revolution, and the rise of consumer culture.

nodes.title: French Postmodern Literature
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.description: This course is devoted to aspects of French poetry, fiction, and film since World War II, beginning with the New Novel and cinematic New Wave and then focusing on more contemporary writers of the late 20th and early 21st century.

nodes.title: Littratures de la Francophonie
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.description: Literature in French by writers outside France. Material includes representative authors and literary movements of Canada, Haiti, Senegal, Zaire, etc. discussion of questions of national identity and literary relations. Lectures and readings in French.

nodes.title: Gender and Sexuality in France
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: One course from French 104A-B-C-E-F, or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: Role of gender and the function of sexuality in the formation of identities in French culture. Themes of family, love, marriage, political and interpersonal relationships in literary texts, films, paintings, and diverse media.

nodes.title: French and Francophone Cinema
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: One course from French 104A-B-C-E-F, or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: Explore French-speaking cinema through a variety of social, geographic and philosophical themes. Topics may include the representation of history, and the counterpoint of text and image. Contents will vary according to the instructor.

nodes.title: Novels on the Screen
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: One course from French 101A-B-C, or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: A comparative study of some of the great French and Francophone novels, alongside their adaptations for the silver screen. What does it mean to adapt a literary text for the cinema? Works studied will include: Balzac, Le colonel Chabert, Flaubert, Madame Bovary, and Zobel, La rue Cases-Ngres, as well as notable adaptations of these works by Angelo, Renoir, Chabrol, Palcy, and others. Lectures and readings in French, films in French (with English subtitles).

nodes.title: Sociology of French Popular Culture
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: One course from French 104A-B-C-E-F, or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: Through the study of sociological essays and popular arts such as films, songs, TV shows, and cartoons, the course examines some features of contemporary France that range from longstanding cultural habits to burning political debates about social mobility, immigration, secularism, globalization, the role of the state, etc. Taught in French.

nodes.title: Globalization and Development in the Francosphere
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.description: Examines the postcolonial history of several Francophone nations in the developing world, emphasizing the interplay between the political, economic, social, and cultural spheres. Specific cases studied will vary. Students develop their own policy-oriented class project. Taught in French.

nodes.title: Bioethics in France and the Francosphere
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: One course from French 104A-B-C-E-F, or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: An introduction to pressing contemporary issues and debates concerning bioethics in France and the Francosphere. Discusses issues such as euthanasia, genetic engineering, artificial intelligence, animal experiments and transhumanism, and culminates in the presentation and defense of student-devised projects. Taught in French.

nodes.title: French for Life and Social Sciences
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: French 6, 6GS, or equivalent.
nodes.description: Project-based course designed to introduce students with an interest in life and/or social sciences to discipline-specific vocabulary and professional conventions necessary to communicate effectively with French speakers in the life and social sciences, including biology, psychology, and medicine. Students work in groups on a collaborative project of their design under the guidance of the instructor, resulting in an oral and written report. Final projects are presented in an event open to fellow students and professors. All sessions are conducted in French, and all work is to be completed in French.

nodes.title: Learning French: Culture, Language, Methods
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: One course from French 104A-B-C-E-F or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: Covers three basic areas important to students interested in language acquisition, particularly for French. These include 1) the interpretation of culturally embedded visual, written, and oral texts; 2) the analysis of French linguistic structure; 3) the psychology of language learning and effective pedagogical methods. Emphasis on intercultural communication and semiotic interpretation. Taught in French.

nodes.title: French for International Relations and Diplomacy
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: One course from French 104A-B-C-E-F or equivalent (may be taken concurrently with instructor's approval).
nodes.description: This course focuses on French perspectives of two organizations dedicated to international relations, the United Nations and the European Union. The analysis of both organizations, which have very different goals, institutions, and agendas, lays the groundwork for an exploration of French diplomatic relations. Students engage in two "model UN" and "model EU" activities for increased understanding of the finer points of international relations and diplomacy. Studentsalso write two "notes de synthse," essentially short formal papers summarizing a political situation. One midterm and one final exam. Taught in French.

nodes.title: Studies in Medieval Literature
nodes.prereq_text: Writing 2 or upper-division standing.
nodes.description: A study of one or more major medieval works in translation such as The Song of Roland, the romances of Chretien de Troyes, the Lais of Marie de France,or The Romance of the Rose.

nodes.title: French Theatre in Translation
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing.
nodes.description: A study of French theatre through the centuries, considered within the cultural context of the day (Classicism, the Enlightenment, Romanticism, the Absurd, etc). Plays by Molire, Marivaux, Beaumarchais, Hugo, Musset, Ionesco, and Beckett. Lectures and readings in English.

nodes.title: Autobiographies and Life Stories
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing.
nodes.description: Considers autobiographies, memoirs, testimonials, life writing, and other works of narrative fiction and nonfiction often written in the first person. Topics include self-portrait, the portrayal of childhood and family, childhood and youth narratives, women's autobiography, first-person accounts of illness and disability in comics, and more. Texts and course foci vary with the instructor.

nodes.title: Fantasy and the Fantastic
nodes.description: Course explores the creation of a space where a fantastic perception of reality developed and thrived, hesitating between the real and the supernatural, in the intermediate space of the unexplained and unexplainable. Works by Balzac, Poe, Stevenson, James, and Borges.

nodes.title: Existentialist Literature in Translation
nodes.description: How much freedom can you take? The course explores the quandaries of the twentieth-century individual, free and self-created, in the world of responsibilities and attachments. Readings include fiction, drama, and philosophical essays by Jean-Paul Sartre, Albert Camus, Simone de Beauvoir.

nodes.title: Voyages to the Unknown
nodes.prereq_text: Writing 2 or equivalent
nodes.description: The impact of the voyages of discovery on late 15th- and 16th-century Europe. Readings on real and imaginary voyages: Columbus, Cartier, Lery, More, Rabelais, Montaigne.

nodes.title: France in the Seventeenth Century
nodes.prereq_text: Upper division standing or Hist 4B or Hist 2B or Hist 9 or Hist 121C
nodes.description: A focus on the history of France from the reign of Henri IV (1595) to the end of the reign of Louis XIV (1715). Topics include court culture and politics, religious tensions and experiences of French Protestants, natural philosophy, social upheaval and gender relations, French colonial endeavors.

nodes.title: Holocaust in France
nodes.description: Through analysis of testimonies, memoirs, fiction, and film, this course focuses on France under the Nazi occupation. Topics include the Vichy Regime (1940-1945), The Resistance Movement, the Church under Vichy, anti-Semitism, deportations and concentration camp imprisonment, and national memory after World War II.

nodes.title: Time Off in Paris!
nodes.description: Paris and Parisian life in nineteenth- and twentieth-century literature, art and cinema. Drawing upon history, architecture, and art history, we explore the shock of urbanization, the relations between the culture and life of the city, and the rise of avant-garde aesthetics.

nodes.title: Post-Colonial Cultures
nodes.description: Study of fiction from the Caribbean, West Africa, and the Maghreb. Born of the conflict between and hybridization of widely differing cultural traditions, this course provides insights into the vibrancy of contemporary post-colonial societies, the ongoing legacy of colonialism, and the meaning of multiculturalism. In English.

nodes.title: Economic Fictions: Literature, Film, and Theory
nodes.description: How have Western thinkers represented economic concepts since the eighteenth century? Themes may include free market liberalism, labor theories of value, household and family economics, currency/monetary policy, associationism/socialism, globalism/expansionism/colonialism, protectionism, and others. In English.

nodes.title: Medicine and Comedy
nodes.prereq_text: Upper division standing.
nodes.description: Medical comedy? Surgical theater? From ancient Greece through the twenty-first century, doctors, patients, and diseases have been staged for comic and cathartic effect at the same time that they transmit serious medical knowledge: all with a big laugh. In English.

nodes.title: French and Francophone Women Writers
nodes.description: French-speaking women writers from the Middle Ages to the present. Gender and genre, politics and poetics in Marie de France, Lafayette, Stal, Sand, Simone de Beauvoir, Marguerite Duras, Assia Djebar, among other writers. In English.

nodes.title: French Cinema: History and Theory
nodes.description: History of French cinema from 1895-present, covering the silent period, the early classic era, the war years, and the New Wave, with a survey of the major French film theories since the 1920s. In English.

nodes.title: Crossreadings : French and Italian Cultures in Dialogue and Translation
nodes.description: Ever since the Renaissance, when the notion of a national culture had taken hold, the historic, literary and intellectual trajectories of France and Italy have been intimately entangled. Taking a chronological approach from the Renaissance to the post-modern period, this course will embark on a number of comparative readings from these two countries: from Rabelais carnivalesque uptake of Boccaccios humor and vulgarity; to Italys attempt at emulating the French Revolution; to Giuseppe Ungarettis debt to avant-garde literary figures, and more. Our goal will be to reveal that cultures and intellectual traditions exist not in isolation but emerge out of a perpetual conversation withand translation ofeach other. Taught in English.

nodes.title: Enhancement Seminar in French
nodes.prereq_text: Instructor approval and concurrent enrollment in any French Upper Division course taught in English (numbered 153 to 156, and 189) or any UD Comparative Literature course taught by French faculty.

items.text: Instructor approval and any French Upper Division course taught in English (numbered 153 to 156

nodes.description: Designed for French majors or minors (or students with reading fluency in French) enrolled in any French Upper Division course taught in English (numbered from 153 to 156, and 189), or Comparative Literature UD courses taught by French faculty. Students will read materials in French, meet with the instructor to discuss them and complete assignments in French in order to improve their linguistic and cultural fluency.

nodes.title: Honors Independent Studies in French
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; 24 upper-division units in French.
nodes.description: Individual investigations in literary or linguistics fields in fulfillment of Senior Honors Thesis for French Major.

nodes.title: Topics in French and Francophone Studies
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: 3 upper division courses in French, including one course from the 104 series and one course from the 101 series.

requires.text: 3 upper division courses in French and including one course from the 104 series and one course from the 101 series

nodes.description: A seminar dedicated to advanced study of topics of special interest in French and Francophone literary, cultural, or sociological studies. Will lead to research projects and include investigation of theoretical issues. May be repeated for credit if topic changes. Content will vary with each instructor. A full description will be available when offered. In French.

nodes.title: Topics in French and Francophone Studies, Honors Seminar
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: Concurrent enrollment in French 197; honors standing
nodes.description: Eligible students are invited to enroll in the honors section, which is taught by the course instructor. It involves discussion of selected texts, students presentations, and the completion of an independent project on any aspect of the courses chosen theme.

nodes.title: Honors Seminar
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: Consent of instructor; honors standing in the French program.

items.text: honors standing in the French program

nodes.description: This seminar is concurrently offered with graduate seminars or with French 197. It is designed to expand research skills through an investigation of theoretical issues and readings of both literary and critical texts. It involves extensive research, sophisticated analysis, and creative reflection. In French.

groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in French.

items.text: completion of 2 upper-division courses in French

nodes.description: Individual investigations in literary or linguistics fields.

nodes.title: Independent Research Assistance
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: C. Upper-division courses taught in French
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing; completion of 2 upper-division courses in French; consent of instructor.

items.text: completion of 2 upper-division courses in French

nodes.description: Independent research, under the supervision of a consenting faculty member.

nodes.title: World History
nodes.description: Survey of the peoples, cultures, and social, economic, and political systems that have characterized the world's major civilizations in Europe, Asia, Africa, the Americas, and Oceania from 1000 to 1700 CE.

nodes.title: World History
nodes.description: Survey of the peoples, cultures, and social, economic, and political systems that have characterized the world's major civilizations in Europe, Asia, Africa, the Americas, and Oceania from 1700 to present.

nodes.title: Medieval and Early Modern Europe
nodes.description: Survey of the history of Europe in the Medieval and Early Modern periods, 800-1700. Discusses the major social, political, religious, and cultural characteristics and developments of the period, as well as key interactions between Europe and other parts of the world. Weekly discussion sections are an important feature of this course, enabling students to develop and expand upon material presented during the lecture hour.

nodes.title: Modern Europe
nodes.description: Survey of the history of Modern Europe, 1650-present. Discusses the major social, political, religious, and cultural characteristics and developments of the period, as well as key interactions between Europe and other parts of the world. Weekly discussion sections are an important feature of this course, enabling students to develop and expand upon material presented during the lecture hour.

nodes.title: Historical Investigations: Methods and Skills
nodes.description: Through studying a particular topic in history, students gain insight into historical methods and skills. Course designed for freshmen and sophomore history majors or prospective majors. Others may enroll by permission of instructor. Topics vary by quarter and instructor.

nodes.title: France in the Sixteenth Century
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Courses not in French Department
nodes.prereq_text: Hist 2B or 4B or 9 or Upper Division Standing.
nodes.description: Politics, religion, and society and culture in France from the reign of Francois I to Henri IV. Topics include the French Renaissance, religious divisions and civil war, kingship and local authority, family and social hierarchy, and France's relations beyond its borders.

nodes.title: France in the Seventeenth Century
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Courses not in French Department
nodes.prereq_text: Upper division standing or Hist 4B or Hist 2B or Hist 9 or Hist 121C
nodes.description: A focus on the history of France from the reign of Henri IV (1595) to the end of the reign of Louis XIV (1715). Topics include court culture and politics, religious tensions and experiences of French Protestants, natural philosophy, social upheaval and gender relations, French colonial endeavors.

nodes.title: History of the French Empire
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Courses not in French Department
nodes.prereq_text: History 2C or 4C or Upper Division standing
nodes.description: Liberty, equality, fraternity: what does this revolutionary motto mean from a colonial perspective? France, often characterized as the country of human rights, also has a long imperial history that sheds light on key contradictions of modernity: democracy and populism, citizenship and inequality, colorblindness and racism. Countries as different as Canada, Haiti, Algeria, Vietnam, Senegal, India and even the United States share a common French colonial past: how did these French roots of globalization define the world as we know it?

nodes.title: The French Revolution
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Courses not in French Department
nodes.prereq_text: History 2B or 2C or 4B or 4C or upper division standing.
nodes.description: The French Revolution was a globally significant historical event. The ideas of liberty and equality articulated through the storming of the Bastille and Declaration of the Rights of Man were radical and volatile, and the Revolution engendered modern notions of republicanism, democracy and citizenship. This was also, however, a period of war, violence and terror, which incited conflicts and upheaval across the world. We will explore the multiple meanings of the French Revolution, and its enduring global ramifications and legacies.

nodes.title: EMS: Approaches to University Writing for Multilingual Students
nodes.prereq_text: Open to students who have not satisfied the Entry Level Writing Requirement and have a Ling 12 placement or a prerequisite of Ling 3C with a grade of C or better.

requires.text: Open to students who have not satisfied the Entry Level Writing Requirement and have a LING 12 placement or a prerequisite of LING 3C

nodes.description: Principles of critical reading, thinking and writing in the university. Students analyze academic discourse, develop rhetorical strategies for exposition and argument, practice examination writing, and write and revise papers. Completion of C or better meets Entry Level Writing Requirement.

nodes.title: French Social Theory
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: Courses not in French Department
nodes.prereq_text: Upper-division standing.
nodes.description: An examination of major developments in French social theory both from the historical and the thematic point of view. Authors studied may include: Comte, Durkheim, Mauss, Althusser, Foucault, Bourdieu, Sartre, Levi-strauss, and Baudrillard.

nodes.title: Academic Writing
nodes.prereq_text: Satisfaction of the Entry Level Writing requirement or Linguistics 12 with a grade of "C" or better.

items.text: Satisfaction of the Entry Level Writing requirement

nodes.description: A writing course focusing on developing analytical skills, synthesizing multiple sources, sustaining coherent arguments, and revising for clarity of style. Reading and writing assignments are drawn from a range of academic disciplines.
